candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — safe insulin storage and pump-supply planning during travel
candidate.educational_objective: When traveling with insulin-pump therapy, keep insulin and essential pump supplies in carry-on luggage, protect insulin from extreme heat and freezing, and plan enough medication and equipment for possible delays.

options.A: I will keep my insulin and pump supplies in my carry-on luggage and protect the insulin from extreme heat and freezing.
options.B: I will pack all insulin in checked luggage because cargo storage keeps medication at a controlled temperature.
options.C: I will place insulin directly against frozen ice packs because freezing does not affect insulin potency.
options.D: I only need the exact amount of insulin for the planned travel time because delays do not affect supply planning.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. FDA guidance for insulin-pump travel advises packing pump supplies, including insulin, in carry-on luggage rather than checked baggage because checked items can be delayed, lost, or damaged. FDA insulin-storage guidance also warns that extreme temperatures reduce insulin effectiveness and specifically states not to use insulin that has been frozen and to keep it away from direct heat and sunlight. C is therefore unsafe. B falsely assumes checked baggage protects medication. D ignores FDA travel guidance to plan adequate medication and supplies for possible travel delays.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Air travelers using insulin pumps should carry insulin and pump supplies in carry-on luggage, plan for travel delays, and protect insulin from extreme heat and freezing because temperature extremes can reduce potency.
candidate.source_document_title: Insulin Pumps: Tips for Using Your Insulin Pump at Home; Information Regarding Insulin Storage and Switching Between Products in an Emergency
candidate.source_locator: FDA Insulin Pumps, ‘Traveling with your insulin pump — Airplane travel’: always pack pump supplies, including insulin, in carry-on luggage; Foreign travel: plan enough medicine for trip and delays and review storage requirements. FDA Insulin Storage and Effectiveness: extreme temperatures reduce effectiveness; avoid freezing; do not use frozen insulin; keep away from direct heat and sunlight
candidate.stem: A client who uses an insulin pump is preparing for air travel. Which statement shows correct understanding of insulin and pump-supply storage?
